subject: Decision Making
title: The Insurance Revolution
description: A 60-second lesson on The Insurance Revolution.

hook.text: Lloyd's of London started in a coffee shop in 1688. Merchants bet on whether ships would survive their voyages.

buildup.text: Ship owners paid a premium. If the ship sank, investors covered the loss. Risk became a tradeable commodity.

discovery.text: Insurance turned probability math into a business. By pooling risk across many ships, losses became predictable.

twist.text: Insurance created moral hazard. If you are covered, you may take more risks than you otherwise would.

climax.text: Insurance proved that uncertainty itself has a price. That insight built the entire modern financial system.

punchline.text: Price the risk, sell the safety. Insurance made uncertainty a product.

quiz.question: What is moral hazard in insurance?
options: Taking more risks because you're covered against loss
